text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil prices spiked on escalating geopolitical risk in the Middle East. Iran intensified attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz on Friday, a critical chokepoint for global oil supplies, sending U.S. crude up sharply. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher revenues and profits — the company benefits immediately when the commodity it extracts sells for more.

The stock's two-week surge of 15.6% reflects a broader rally in oil prices driven by Middle East tensions, compounded by tight global supply. A separate dynamic worth noting: physical oil delivery costs have surged due to elevated tanker rates, meaning the "real" cost to get oil to market is running roughly $30–$40 per barrel above the headline price — a headwind for refiners but a tailwind for upstream producers like ConocoPhillips that don't bear those transport costs.
